title: Al-Fattah, the Opener
hook: the Opener, of doors, of hearts, of ways out

segments.voice: Yesterday, Ar-Razzaq: the birds out hungry and back full, and the camel tied. Your line was provided for.

Remember Hudaybiyyah, eleven days ago, where the name ar-Rahman was struck from the treaty's first line? The rest of it felt worse. The Muslims had come to visit the Ka'ba and were sent home without reaching it. Some of the terms looked one-sided. Many companions were deeply upset; Umar, Bukhari records, went to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ asking why they should accept such terms. They rode back toward Medina with their heads down. On the way, a surah came down, and its first line called that treaty a clear victory. The Arabic word for victory there is the same word as opening.
screen: `SENT HOME FROM MECCA.` → `A TREATY THAT FELT LIKE A LOSS.` → `CALLED A CLEAR VICTORY.`

segments.voice: Inna fatahna laka fathan mubina. The first line of Surah al-Fath: We have opened for you a clear opening, a clear victory. The root is f-t-h, to open. It gives miftah, a key. It gives fath, an opening, and a victory, because a victory is a way through. And it gives the name of the first surah you learned: al-Fatiha, the opening. The treaty that looked like a door slamming turned out to be a door opening: two years of peace, in which, historians say, more people entered Islam than in all the years before. Al-Fattah is the one who opens. In Surah Saba' the name has a second shade: our Lord will bring us together, then He will open between us with truth, and He is al-Fattah, al-'Alim, the Opener, the All-Knowing. Here opening means judging: laying a dispute open so the truth is seen. In Surah Fatir, whatever mercy Allah opens for people, no one can hold back; whatever He holds back, no one can release. In al-An'am: with Him are the keys of the unseen. So the name covers every kind of stuck: a locked door, a locked-up heart, a dispute no one can settle, a way out you can't see. Entering a mosque, many Muslims say words the Prophet taught, recorded by Muslim: O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy. The one entering asks; the opening is left to al-Fattah.
screen: `FATH — AN OPENING, A VICTORY.` · `MIFTAH, FATH, AL-FATIHA.` · `OPENING THE TRUTH BETWEEN PEOPLE.` · `THE KEYS OF THE UNSEEN.` · then, large: `THE OPENER.`

segments.voice: Name one thing in your life that feels stuck, a conversation going nowhere, a job search, a friendship gone cold, something in you that won't budge, and picture it as a closed door. Don't push on it; stand in front of it, breathe, and let not holding the key be a relief instead of a fear. If you pray, you can ask Allah, al-Fattah, to open it, or to open another way you haven't seen.
Al-Fattah. The Opener, of doors, hearts and ways out, and the one who opens the truth between people. Today's word.
Your line: the opener. A treaty that felt like a loss was called a clear opening. Day two hundred forty-six is yours.

howItsDone: Many Muslims say Allahumma iftah li abwaba rahmatik, O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy, when entering a mosque, and call on al-Fattah when a matter is stuck, asking for an opening.

fork.setup: you're riding home from Hudaybiyyah, turned away from Mecca, upset by the terms. what does the surah revealed on the way say?
options: you have been defeated this time
We have opened for you a clear victory
fork.reveal: 48:1: a clear opening, a clear victory. the peace that followed opened far more than it closed.

original.note: Arabic: the Opener, the Judge who lays truth open; from f-t-h, to open.

trapdoor: what you thought: God opens doors for people.
what it means: the Opener of doors, hearts and ways out, and the one who opens the truth between people.
what a scholar hears: f-t-h gives miftah, fath and al-Fatiha; 34:26 pairs al-Fattah al-'Alim; 48:1 names Hudaybiyyah fath mubin; Muslim 713, the mosque du'a.

sources.ref: Qur'an 48:1 (a clear victory, a clear opening)
Qur'an 34:26 (He will open between us with truth; He is al-Fattah, al-'Alim)
Qur'an 35:2; 6:59 (mercy He opens none can withhold; the keys of the unseen)
Sahih Muslim 713 (open for me the doors of Your mercy)

notes: Bukhari 3182 and Muslim 713 cited from memory; confirm numbers.
The claim that more people entered Islam during the Hudaybiyyah truce than before is from classical historians (e.g. al-Zuhri as reported by Ibn Hisham); the script says 'historians say'. Confirm.
Surah al-Fath is generally said to have been revealed on the return from Hudaybiyyah; confirm.
Pickthall's wordings of 48:1, 34:26 and 35:2 are paraphrased, not quoted.
